idea_why: Tool use plus an iterative critique with stored evidence is a well-founded way to lift a fixed model, though the model names suggest the paper needs a careful read.
breakdown: The pattern ports to any perception task: give the model crop, zoom and measure tools, log every finding to a memory file, and have a second pass list gaps before the answer is final. mechanism: UK private medical billing runs through recognition bodies and clearing houses. CCSD recognition is the gate for insurer billing by clinicians, and Healthcode is the electronic claims switch between providers and insurers. Offshore staff handling patient data need an international data transfer agreement (IDTA) under UK GDPR. Insurers and regulators police this through recognition checks and audit of data flows.
claim: The vault note lists CCSD, Healthcode, insurer recognition and IDTA as the requirements for offshore billing work.
why_not_testable: It is regulatory and commercial structure, not software that can be run.
needs: Insurer recognition, a Healthcode account and a signed IDTA.
one_line: UK private medical billing is gated by CCSD recognition, the Healthcode claims switch and an IDTA for offshore staff.
idea_why: The gating requirements are real and explain why the market is hard to enter without a recognised partner.
breakdown: Understanding it means mapping the claim path: clinician, biller, Healthcode, insurer, remittance. The compliance pieces are public documents from the insurers and the ICO, which a research pass can summarise. Any live work needs a hired data protection adviser and a recognised billing partner, because no script can grant recognition.
